subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where `no-new-privileges` prevents even `/usr/bin/sleep` from execing, and should that path be an explicit dangerous opt-out, diagnostic-only guidance, or another security-reviewed fix?
rationale: The observable bug is real, but disabling or falling back from `no-new-privileges` changes the Docker sandbox boundary and AGENTS/VISION policy requires explicit, operator-controlled security tradeoffs rather than silent compatibility fallbacks.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` enabled by default, add a clearly named config key with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

options.title: Diagnostic-only handling
options.body: Keep the hardening unconditional and improve startup/session/doctor errors so affected hosts get a precise explanation and mitigation guidance without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Reject opt-out
options.body: Treat hosts where Docker rejects `no-new-privileges` as unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to another sandbox backend or host configuration.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` enabled by default, add a clearly named config key with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history on sandbox security/config override patterns that this decision would extend.
